title: Netra access-code exchange: POST /v1/device-credentials
$comment: Decision D-CRED (20 September 2026). An operator issues each student a one-time access code; the desktop app exchanges it once, over HTTPS, for a device credential it keeps in Windows Credential Manager and presents as `Authorization: Bearer` on /v1/ws and the HTTP routes. The route takes no credential. Responses: 201 with CredentialIssued; otherwise {"error": <protocol/v1/error.schema.json>} with 422 INVALID_REQUEST (malformed body or code format), 401 AUTH_REQUIRED (the code is unknown, expired, revoked or already used, all indistinguishable so codes cannot be probed) or 503 RESOURCE_UNAVAILABLE (retry later with the same request_id). Replay: if the response is lost, the client resends the same access_code with the same request_id; within 15 minutes of the first exchange the server issues a fresh credential and revokes the earlier one, so exactly one credential from a code is ever live. A different request_id, or a resend after 15 minutes, gets 401.

access_code.$comment: As typed. The server ignores case, spaces and hyphens and reads O as 0 and I or L as 1; what remains must be 12 characters of Crockford base32 (0-9 and A-Z without I, L, O, U), about 60 bits. Codes are shown as three groups of four, for example 7K3Q-M9TX-2BWD.

request_id.$comment: Minted once per exchange attempt and reused verbatim on retransmission.

credential.$comment: Opaque bearer token. Stored only in Windows Credential Manager; never logged, displayed or put in a URL. The server keeps only its SHA-256 digest.

expires_at.$comment: The operator chose the credential lifetime when issuing the code. After it, or after revocation, the app needs a new access code.
